name: reset
description: Start the current bar of a pattern again whenever a trigger happens.
notes: Give a trigger pattern, such as x ~ x ~. Each x starts it again; ~ leaves a gap. This is not a count of bars.

name: restart
description: Start the whole pattern again from its first bar whenever a trigger happens.
notes: Give a trigger pattern, such as x ~ x ~. Unlike reset, this also returns a pattern that spans several bars to its first bar.

name: invert
description: Swap the on and off values in a pattern: 0 becomes 1, and 1 becomes 0.
notes: Use with a pattern of on/off values, such as a rhythm mask. It does not turn a melody upside down.

name: pick
description: Use numbers or names to choose from a list of patterns, keeping each chosen pattern's timing.
notes: Start with a pattern of choice numbers and supply a list of choices. List positions start at 0; a number past the end selects the last choice.
Use this inside a named pattern or signal, then pass its result to notes: or play:. A plain number after pick: is not a choices list.
example:
signal: choices
  run: 2
  pick: ["C4 E4", "G4 B4"]
track: melody
  sound: triangle
  notes: $choices

name: pickmod
description: Choose a pattern by number, starting again at the first choice when the number passes the end of the list.
notes: Use a pattern of choice numbers and a list of patterns, as with pick. List positions start at 0.

name: pick f
description: Use numbers to choose which change to apply to your music.
notes: Give the choice numbers, then a list of changes. List positions start at 0. Use $name to refer to a change: block you defined.
For example, 0, [rev, rev] selects the first of two reverse changes. Use different named changes to make the choices useful.

name: pickmod f
description: Choose a change by number, starting again at the first choice when the number passes the end of the list.
notes: In this app’s current engine, give the list of changes first, then the number pattern. This argument order differs from pick f.
List positions start at 0. Larger choice numbers wrap back to the start of the list.

name: pick restart
description: Choose a pattern and start it again from its first bar each time it is selected.
notes: Needs a pattern of choice numbers and a list of choices, just like pick. List positions start at 0.

name: pickmod restart
description: Choose and restart a pattern, returning to the first choice when the choice number passes the end of the list.
notes: Needs a pattern of choice numbers and a list of choices. List positions start at 0.

name: pick reset
description: Choose a pattern and start its current bar again each time it is selected.
notes: Needs a pattern of choice numbers and a list of choices. Use pick restart if you also want to return to the first bar.

name: pickmod reset
description: Choose a pattern and restart its current bar, returning to the first choice when the choice number passes the list's end.
notes: Needs a pattern of choice numbers and a list of choices. List positions start at 0.

name: inhabit
description: Choose patterns and fit one bar of each into the time taken by its choice event.
notes: Needs a pattern of choice numbers and a list of patterns, just like pick. A shorter choice event makes the chosen pattern play faster.

name: inhabitmod
description: Choose patterns and fit them into each choice event, wrapping back to the first choice after the end of the list.
notes: Needs a pattern of choice numbers and a list of patterns. List positions start at 0.

name: squeeze
description: Choose a pattern by number and fit it into the time taken by that choice.
notes: This function needs a pattern of choice numbers and a list of choices. Use inhabitmod for the same kind of choice as a command inside a signal block.
example:
signal: choices
  run: 2
track: melody
  sound: triangle
  notes: squeeze($choices, ["C4 E4", "G4 B4"])

name: superimpose
description: Play the original pattern together with a changed copy.
notes: Indent the changes beneath this command, such as faster: 2 or transpose: 12. Both copies play, so check their combined volume.

name: layer
description: Add a changed copy of the pattern on top of the original.
notes: In this app, indent the changes beneath layer:. It keeps the original playing, like superimpose.

name: off
description: Add a changed copy that starts later or earlier than the original.
notes: Give the time shift in bars: 0.25 is a quarter of a bar later. Indent the changes beneath this command.

name: echo
description: Play several copies with a gap between them, making each later copy quieter.
notes: Give the total number of copies, the gap in bars, and a volume multiplier. For example, 3, 0.125, 0.5 gives three copies, spaced one eighth of a bar apart, each half as loud as the last.

name: echo with
description: Play several copies spaced apart in time, using the changes you choose.
notes: Give the total number of copies and the gap in bars, then indent the changes underneath. The changes apply to every copy, including the first.

name: add
description: Add the given number to each number in a pattern.
notes: Use on number patterns or signals. To move the pitch of notes already in a track, use transpose.

name: sub
description: Subtract the given number from each number in a pattern.
notes: Use on number patterns or signals. To lower notes already in a track, use transpose with a negative number.

name: mul
description: Multiply each number in a pattern by the given amount. Multiplying by 2 doubles it.
notes: Use on number patterns or signals, before passing the result to a setting such as frequency or volume.

name: div
description: Divide each number in a pattern by the given amount. Dividing by 2 halves it.
notes: Use on number patterns or signals. The amount must not be zero.

name: round
description: Round each number to the nearest whole number. For example, 2.7 becomes 3.
notes: Use on a number pattern or signal, such as moving values that will become note numbers.

name: floor
description: Round each number down to a whole number. For example, 2.7 becomes 2.
notes: Use on number patterns or signals. Negative numbers also round downward: -2.3 becomes -3.

name: ceil
description: Round each number up to a whole number. For example, 2.3 becomes 3.
notes: Use on number patterns or signals. Negative numbers also round upward: -2.7 becomes -2.

name: range
description: Change values from 0–1 into a range you choose. With 200, 2000, a value of 0 becomes 200 and 1 becomes 2000.
notes: Pairs with signals such as sine and rand. Use range2 for signals that go from -1 to 1.

name: rangex
description: Change values from 0–1 into a range where equal steps multiply the result by equal amounts.
notes: Give two positive limits. This is useful for a signal controlling frequency, where multiplying by 2 raises the pitch by one octave.

name: range2
description: Change values from -1–1 into a range you choose. The middle value, 0, maps to the middle of your range.
notes: Pairs with signals such as sine2 and rand2. Use range for signals that go from 0 to 1.

name: ratio
description: Turn ratios into numbers. For example, 3:2 becomes 1.5.
notes: Use on a pattern containing ratios. You can multiply the result by a starting frequency to make related pitches.

name: as
description: Give values the names of the settings they should control, such as note or gain.
notes: Use on plain values before they become sound events. Give a setting name, or a list of native setting names that matches the order of the values.

name: sine
description: Make a number that rises and falls smoothly between 0 and 1, once per bar.
notes: Put it inside a signal: block, then use $name in a setting such as lowpass:. Add range: to choose the lowest and highest values. For a sine instrument, use sound: sine.

name: cosine
description: Make a number that starts at 1 and smoothly falls to 0 and rises again, once per bar.
notes: Use inside a named signal, then pass $name to a sound setting. Add range: to choose its limits.

name: saw
description: Make a number that steadily rises from 0 toward 1, then jumps back to 0 each bar.
notes: Use inside a named signal and add range: to choose useful limits. This controls a number; sound: sawtooth chooses an instrument.

name: tri
description: Make a number that rises from 0 to 1 and falls back at a steady speed each bar.
notes: Use inside a named signal and add range: to choose useful limits. For a triangle instrument, use sound: triangle.

name: square
description: Make a number that switches between 0 and 1 halfway through each bar.
notes: Use inside a named signal to switch a setting between two values. For a square instrument, use sound: square.

name: rand
description: Make a random number between 0 and 1 whenever the pattern reads it.
notes: Use inside a named signal. Add range: to choose limits, or segment: to choose how many separate values happen per bar.

name: perlin
description: Make random values between 0 and 1 that change smoothly over time.
notes: Use inside a named signal. Pair with range: and a setting such as lowpass: for gradual changes in sound.

name: irand
description: Make random whole numbers starting at 0 and stopping just before the number you give. With 4, the choices are 0, 1, 2, and 3.
notes: Use a positive whole number. Add segment: to create separate steps, then use the numbers for choices or scale notes.

name: brand
description: Randomly choose true or false, with an equal chance of each.
notes: Use as an on/off signal, such as a mask that decides which notes play.

name: brand by
description: Randomly choose true or false, using the chance you give for true.
notes: Use a value from 0 to 1, or a percentage. For example, 25% gives true about one quarter of the time.

name: time
description: Make a number showing how many bars have passed, including part of the current bar.
notes: Use inside a signal: block. Its value keeps increasing, so use math or another change if your sound setting needs a limited range.

name: signal
description: Name a changing number that you can use to control a sound setting.
notes: Put signal: at the left edge and indent a source such as sine: beneath it. Use $ followed by the signal's name in another command.
example:
signal: sweep
  sine:
  range: 300, 2000
track: melody
  sound: triangle
  notes: C4 E4 G4
  lowpass: $sweep

name: mousex
description: Make a changing number from the mouse pointer's left-to-right position.
notes: Use inside a named signal and pass it to a sound setting. Playback and an exported file can differ if you move the mouse.

name: mousey
description: Make a changing number from the mouse pointer's up-and-down position.
notes: Use inside a named signal and pass it to a sound setting. Playback and an exported file can differ if you move the mouse.

name: pace
description: Set how many pattern steps fit into one bar.
notes: Needs a pattern with counted steps. Pairs with stepcat, expand, contract, extend, take, drop, shrink, grow, tour, and zip.

name: stepalt
description: Join patterns step by step, taking turns between the choices in each list.
notes: Give patterns or lists of alternatives. Add pace: afterward to choose how many steps play per bar.

name: expand
description: Multiply the pattern's counted number of steps by the amount you give.
notes: This affects timing when used with pace: or a command that joins counted steps. It does not slow playback on its own; use slower: for that.

name: contract
description: Divide the pattern's counted number of steps by the amount you give.
notes: This affects timing when used with pace: or a command that joins counted steps. Use a positive amount.

name: extend
description: Repeat the pattern more times and increase its step count to match.
notes: With extend: 2, A B becomes A B A B. Pair with pace: or stepcat to use the new step count.

name: take
description: Keep only the number of steps you choose.
notes: A positive number keeps steps from the start; a negative number keeps them from the end. Needs a pattern with counted steps.

name: drop
description: Remove the number of steps you choose and keep the rest.
notes: A positive number removes steps from the start; a negative number removes them from the end. Needs a pattern with counted steps.

name: shrink
description: Play a series of shorter versions of the pattern, removing steps each time.
notes: A positive amount removes steps from the start; a negative amount removes them from the end. Add pace: to set the speed of the resulting steps.

name: grow
description: Play a series of longer versions, adding steps until the whole pattern plays.
notes: A positive amount grows from the start; a negative amount grows from the end. Add pace: to set the speed of the resulting steps.

name: tour
description: Insert this pattern among other patterns, moving it one place earlier on each repeat.
notes: Give the other patterns as arguments. All these repeats fit into one bar unless you add pace: to spread out the steps.

name: zip
description: Take one step from each pattern in turn and repeat that order.
notes: Needs patterns with counted steps, rather than a plain number. Add pace: to spread the resulting steps across bars.
example:
signal: interleaved
  zip: mini("C4 E4"), mini("G4 A4")
  pace: 4
track: melody
  sound: triangle
  notes: $interleaved

name: color
description: Choose the color of your notes in the music display, such as red or #7042bf.
notes: Put it inside a track. It changes note drawings; waveform and spectrum show the combined sound.

name: piano roll
description: Show notes as bars: their height shows pitch and their width shows length.

name: punchcard
description: Show when the pattern's notes and sounds happen as marks in a grid.

name: spiral
description: Show the pattern's notes and sounds moving around a spiral.

name: waveform
description: Show a moving line shaped by the sound playing now.
notes: Shows the combined audio from the song. Start playback to see the line move.

name: pitch wheel
description: Show note pitches around a circle so you can see which notes are playing.

name: spectrum
description: Show how much of the sound is low, middle, or high pitched.
notes: Shows the combined audio from the song. Start playback to see it change.

name: markcss
description: This display styling command is not available in this app.
notes: Use color: to choose note colors.

name: log
description: This command for printing pattern details is not available in this app.
notes: Use the music display to inspect notes and their timing.

name: midi
description: Send notes to another music app or instrument through a connection called MIDI.
notes: Not available in this app yet; planned for a later release.

name: midin
description: Read messages from a connected MIDI controller, such as its knobs and buttons.
notes: Not available in this app yet; planned for a later release.

name: midikeys
description: Read the notes you press on a connected MIDI keyboard.
notes: Not available in this app yet; planned for a later release.

name: midiport
description: Choose which connected MIDI device receives the music.
notes: Not available in this app yet; planned for a later release.

name: midichan
description: Choose a MIDI channel, which lets one connection control different instrument parts.
notes: Not available in this app yet; planned for a later release.

name: midicmd
description: Send start, stop, and timing messages to other MIDI music equipment.
notes: Not available in this app yet; planned for a later release.

name: osc
description: Send music events to another app using a connection called Open Sound Control, or OSC.
notes: Not available in this app yet; planned for a later release.

name: every
description: Apply a change every chosen number of bars.
notes: Give a positive whole number and indent the change beneath it. For example, every: 4 with faster: 2 doubles the pattern's speed every fourth bar.

name: stut
description: An older command for repeating a pattern with quieter copies.
notes: Use echo: for new music. Here the values are copy count, volume multiplier, then gap in bars; echo puts the gap before the volume multiplier.

name: sine2
description: Make a number that smoothly rises and falls between -1 and 1, once per bar.
notes: Use inside a named signal. Add range2: to choose useful limits before passing it to a sound setting.

name: cosine2
description: Make a number that starts at 1, smoothly falls to -1, and rises again each bar.
notes: Use inside a named signal. Add range2: to choose useful limits before passing it to a sound setting.

name: saw2
description: Make a number that steadily rises from -1 toward 1, then jumps back to -1 each bar.
notes: Use inside a named signal. Add range2: to choose useful limits before passing it to a sound setting.

name: tri2
description: Make a number that rises from -1 to 1 and falls back at a steady speed each bar.
notes: Use inside a named signal. Add range2: to choose useful limits before passing it to a sound setting.

name: square2
description: Make a number that switches between -1 and 1 halfway through each bar.
notes: Use inside a named signal. Add range2: to choose the two values you want to switch between.

name: rand2
description: Make a random number between -1 and 1 whenever the pattern reads it.
notes: Use inside a named signal. Add range2: to choose limits, or segment: to create separate steps.

name: perlin2
description: Make random values between -1 and 1 that change smoothly over time.
notes: Use inside a named signal. Add range2: to choose useful limits before passing it to a sound setting.

description: Put this between choices in a pattern to pick one at random.
notes: Use inside a notes: or play: value, such as C4 | E4 | G4.

description: Strudel uses backticks around patterns that span several lines.
notes: In this app, keep each command's value on one line. You do not need backticks around notes: or play: values.

name: tempo
description: Set the song's speed in beats per minute. At 120 bpm, two beats pass each second.
notes: Put it at the left edge to set the song's speed, or inside a section: to change speed there. Use a number greater than zero.

name: beats per bar
description: Choose how many beats make one bar, a repeating group of beats.
notes: Put it at the left edge. With 4 beats per bar, count 1, 2, 3, 4 before the next bar starts.

name: track
description: Start one musical part, such as drums, bass, or melody.
notes: Give the track a unique name and indent its commands underneath. Tracks play together unless your arrangement chooses only some of them.

name: play
description: Write the sounds and rests that play across one bar.
notes: Use loaded sound names, such as kick and snare. Spaces divide the bar evenly; rest leaves a gap. Put this inside a track.

name: show
description: Choose how the app draws your music while it plays.
notes: Choose piano roll, punchcard, spiral, pitch wheel, waveform, or spectrum.

name: section
description: Name a part of your song, such as intro or chorus.
notes: Put it inside arrange:. Indent bars: and tracks: underneath to choose its length and the parts that play.

name: bars
description: Set how many bars this section lasts.
notes: Put it inside a section: block. Use a positive whole number, such as 8.

name: tracks
description: Choose which named tracks play during this section.
notes: Put it inside a section: block and use names from your track: blocks. Separate names with spaces.

name: pattern
description: Name musical instructions so you can use them again.
notes: Put a named pattern at the left edge and indent its instructions. Use use: followed by its name inside a track.

name: change
description: Name a group of changes so you can apply them again.
notes: Put it at the left edge and indent changes such as lowpass: beneath it. Apply it with use:, or pass $name where a command asks for a change.

name: use
description: Apply a pattern or change that you named in your song.
notes: The name must match a pattern: or change: definition. Put use: inside the track or definition where you want those instructions applied.
